name: Early Dynastic Period
description: Egypt's first national state emerged when Pharaoh Narmer unified Upper and Lower Egypt around 3100 BCE. This period established the foundations of pharaonic civilization: divine kingship, bureaucracy, and monumental architecture. Memphis became the capital, and writing evolved to record royal deeds.
description_ar: ظهرت أول دولة قومية مصرية عندما وحد الفرعون نارمر مصر العليا والسفلى حوالي 3100 قبل الميلاد. أرسى هذا العصر أسس الحضارة الفرعونية: الملكية الإلهية والبيروقراطية والعمارة الضخمة.

name: Old Kingdom
description: The Age of Pyramids. Dynasties 3-6 witnessed humanity's most ambitious architectural projects. From Djoser's revolutionary Step Pyramid (c. 2670 BCE) to Khufu's Great Pyramid (c. 2560 BCE), pharaohs commanded the construction of colossal tombs to ensure eternal life. Imhotep pioneered stone architecture; Egyptian engineering reached unprecedented heights. Central authority peaked, but by Dynasty 6, provincial governors gained power, leading to gradual political fragmentation.
description_ar: عصر الأهرامات. شهدت الأسرات 3-6 أكثر المشاريع المعمارية طموحاً للبشرية. من هرم دجوسر المدرج الثوري إلى الهرم الأكبر لخوفو، أمر الفراعنة ببناء قبور ضخمة.

name: First Intermediate Period
description: After the Old Kingdom's collapse, centralized authority crumbled. Provincial governors became independent, and Egypt fractured into competing regions. Famine and instability plagued the land. Yet this period wasn't entirely chaotic—local administrators developed independent cultural traditions. Nubian influence increased in the south. This fragmentation would eventually catalyze reunion under stronger dynasties.
description_ar: بعد انهيار الدولة القديمة، تفتت السلطة المركزية. أصبح الحكام الإقليميون مستقلين، وانقسمت مصر إلى مناطق متنافسة. الجوع وعدم الاستقرار ساد البلاد.

name: Middle Kingdom
description: A renaissance of art, literature, and architecture. Egypt experienced renewed prosperity and cultural achievements under strong pharaohs like Amenemhat III. This was Egypt's classical age: literature flourished, temples were rebuilt, and administrators established stable governance. Nubia was brought under Egyptian control; trade expanded throughout the Mediterranean and Near East. Yet this stability was threatened by Asiatic peoples entering the delta.
description_ar: نهضة الفن والأدب والعمارة. شهدت مصر ازدهاراً متجدداً وإنجازات ثقافية تحت فراعنة أقويـاء. كان هذا العصر الذهبي الكلاسيكي لمصر.

name: Second Intermediate Period
description: Foreign invasion and rule by the Hyksos (Asiatic peoples, likely from Syria-Palestine). The Hyksos established themselves in the Delta, introducing new military technologies (horses, chariots, composite bows). Though often portrayed as devastating, Hyksos rule was administratively sophisticated. Egyptian independence was eventually restored by the Theban kings of Dynasty 17, who allied with Nubian kingdoms. This period set the stage for the New Kingdom's imperial expansion.
description_ar: غزو أجنبي والحكم من قبل الهكسوس. أسس الهكسوس أنفسهم في الدلتا، وأدخلوا تقنيات عسكرية جديدة. تم استعادة الاستقلال المصري في النهاية من قبل ملوك طيبة.

name: New Kingdom - Early (18th Dynasty)
description: Egypt's Imperial Age. Pharaohs like Ahmose, Hatshepsut, Thutmose III, and Amenhotep III expanded Egyptian dominion to its greatest territorial extent. Luxor and Karnak temples were built; Valley of the Kings became the royal necropolis. This era epitomized New Kingdom magnificence—art, architecture, and literature achieved new heights. Women had more rights; trade flourished. The period saw the anomaly of Akhenaten's monotheistic revolution before Tutankhamun restored traditional religion.
description_ar: العصر الذهبي لمصر. وسّع الفراعنة السيطرة المصرية إلى أقصى امتداد إقليمي. بُنيت معابد الأقصر والكرنك؛ أصبح وادي الملوك المقبرة الملكية.

name: New Kingdom - Late (19th-20th Dynasty)
description: Continued imperial power under Ramesses II (the Great), who ruled 66 years and built Abu Simbel. Ramesses III defended against Sea Peoples invasions. Yet cracks appeared: inflation, labor unrest (first recorded strikes), and priestly power grew. By Dynasty 20's end, pharaonic authority weakened. However, this period produced Egypt's greatest monuments and maintained cultural continuity. It was the last gasp of true pharaonic dominance.
description_ar: استمرار القوة الإمبراطورية تحت رمسيس الثاني العظيم، الذي حكم 66 سنة وبنى أبو سمبل.
highlights: Ramesses III defends against Sea Peoples

name: Third Intermediate Period
description: Declining central authority and political fragmentation. Egypt split into competing power centers: pharaohs in the north; high priests of Amun in the south. Foreign powers increased influence. Yet despite political fragmentation, Egyptian culture remained strong. Libyan mercenaries became influential; Egyptian identity endured. This period set the stage for conquest by outside powers but also demonstrated Egyptian cultural resilience.
description_ar: تراجع السلطة المركزية والتفتت السياسي. انقسمت مصر إلى مراكز قوة متنافسة: فراعنة في الشمال؛ كهنة آمون في الجنوب.

name: Late Period
description: Egypt was ruled by foreign powers (especially Persia), though native dynasties sometimes regained control. The 26th Dynasty (Saite Period) saw a cultural renaissance—ancient traditions were revived, temples restored, and trade flourished. Yet the era was marked by periodic invasions and foreign occupation. Despite this, Egyptian identity remained strong, and the people maintained religious and cultural traditions passed down through millennia.
description_ar: حكمت مصر قوى أجنبية (خاصة فارس)، على الرغم من أن الأسرات الأصلية حكمت في بعض الأحيان.

name: Ptolemaic & Greco-Roman Periods
description: Alexander the Great conquered Egypt in 332 BCE, ending native pharaonic rule. His general Ptolemy founded the Ptolemaic Dynasty (Greek rulers who adopted Egyptian customs). Cleopatra VII was the last pharaoh—a brilliant diplomat who attempted to preserve Egyptian independence against Rome. After her death in 30 BCE, Egypt became a Roman province. Yet Egyptian culture, religion, and traditions persisted even under foreign rule, surviving into the Christian era and influencing Mediterranean civilization.
description_ar: فتح الإسكندر الأكبر مصر في 332 قبل الميلاد، منهياً الحكم الفرعوني الأصلي. أسس جنرالها بطليموس الأسرة البطلمية.
